messages:
jin: Heads-up — I pushed PR #4128 (kv-cache: lazy-evict + minor GC tweak). Quick perf note: local long-seq benchmark shows a p95 bump. Pinging reviewers for a quick look before merge. https://github.com/redwood-inference/repo/pull/4128 :eyes:

maria: on it. do you have the bench output? curious about memory too.

jin: pasted the run below (ran on perf-amber, 8xA10G):
```
Benchmark: long-seq-16k
- prev (main): p50 118ms, p95 420ms, rss 6.3GB
- this PR:   p50 125ms, p95 890ms, rss 7.4GB
- notes: throughput steady, but p95 doubled for long sequences
```
I suspect the lazy-evict path is adding synchronous work under certain KV patterns.

alex: ugh that's a pretty clear regression at p95. did perf-ci run?

perf-bot: CI perf run finished for PR #4128 — 3 regressions detected. Details: https://ci.redwood/4128/artifacts (summary: long-seq-16k p95 +470ms, mem RSS +1.1GB).

sam: @jin can you show the small diff for the eviction path? maybe it's acquiring the global lock more frequently.

jin: short diff snippet:
```diff
- if (kv.size() > limit) evict_oldest();
+ if (kv.size() > limit) {
+   acquire(evict_lock);
+   evict_lazy_batch();
+   release(evict_lock);
+ }
```
I added a per-shard lazy batcher to avoid evicting on the hot path; maybe the lock is contended for long sequences.

maria: if the lock causes stalls, p95 will spike but p50/throughput might remain. can you run a flamegraph on a failing trace?

jin: yes will capture. quick repro: run `./perf/run_long_seq.sh --seq-len 16k --concurrency 8` — the trace is at /tmp/trace4128.tar.gz on the perf box.

alex: my suggestion: revert the lock change and instead enqueue keys to a background worker with lock-free ring buffer. cheap to prototype. if that's quick, do it and rerun CI.

sam: +1. also verify KV cache hit rate didn't change (maybe eviction strategy changed timings).

jin: agreed, I'll push a revert/prototype in a follow-up commit. timeline: can do a patch by EOD. If CI still fails we should hold merge.

maria: also add an automated check to perf CI that compares p95 for long-seq within 10% of baseline. we've had noisy regressions here before.

perf-bot: noted — adding test ticket: PERF-171 to triage long-seq p95 gating.

deploy-bot: reminder — there is a scheduled canary for main tonight at 23:00 UTC. if we merge a change, we should coordinate rollback playbook.

alex: ok. @jin once you have the revert PR, tag me and i'll do a quick review. if passing CI + no mem bump, we can merge and target midnight canary.

jin: thanks all — pushing a revert now, will post the new PR link here. :thumbsup:
